So the fact gate refused all new content for this product on the strength of a disagreement that did not exist. Re-statused to verified against three fetches made today: api.github.com ("private": false, MIT), an anonymous raw.githubusercontent.com read (HTTP 200, 14,048 bytes, byte-identical to the origin), and registry.npmjs.org/@kynth%2Ftearline (HTTP 200, 0.1.0).

THE CORRECTION HAD MISSED THREE SURFACES, one of them live body copy. /share-image-custom-element told readers "the repository is private, so the source cannot be read on GitHub" — a false claim about our own product, under a heading advising when to choose a competitor. SiteHeader.tsx justified its absent GitHub link with a 404 that no longer happens. /docs — the install reference — still said the script tag was the only path because "the package is not published", and had no npm line anywhere on it. All three fixed; /docs gains `npm i @kynth/tearline` and a link to the public MIT source. Grep now finds no surviving "private"/"cannot be read" assertion anywhere in src/, public/llms.txt or README.md.

A SECOND, QUIETER DRIFT WAS CAUGHT ON THE WAY. 4f2b21d grew the component 14,048 -> 17,991 bytes (370 -> 426 lines) and did not move the four page citations of the old figure. They would have gone false the instant it deployed. Moved to 17,991 here so copy and component land in the same deploy batch. The live origin still served 14,048 while this was written — that is the pre-deploy state, and it is recorded as such rather than papered over.

AND ONE FINDING THAT IS NOT FIXED IN THE REPO, BECAUSE IT CANNOT BE. The published npm manifest for @kynth/tearline@0.1.0 has NO `repository` and NO `bugs` field — 4f2b21d added both to ops/npm/package.json, but 0.1.0 was published hours earlier and npm versions are immutable. So npmjs.com still shows no source link. It ships on the next publish, which ops/npm/publish.mjs correctly refuses to run until the site deploys, because the staged component (17,991) does not yet match the live origin (14,048). Recorded on npm-package-published; no repo change can close it.

CRAWL STATE improved: 4 of 7 URLs unknown to Google today against 6 of 7 yesterday, /docs and /dom-to-png back to "Discovered". Indexed still 0. Two readings a day apart on a cold host are noise around a trend and are recorded, not narrated — see sitemap.ts. NO NEW PAGE SHIPPED: the fact gate was blocking, which is exactly what it is for.

⚠ THE PUBLISHED MANIFEST HAS NO `repository` AND NO `bugs` FIELD. Commit 4f2b21d added both to ops/npm/package.json and its message reports npm as fixed — but 0.1.0 was published BEFORE that edit, and an npm version is immutable. Read off the packument today: `versions["0.1.0"].repository` is undefined and the top-level `repository` is undefined. So npmjs.com/package/@kynth/tearline still shows no Repository link, for a package whose entire pitch is one readable file. The fix is staged on disk and ships only on the next publish; nothing in the repo asserts otherwise as of this commit. This is the source-file-vs-primary-source gap in miniature: ops/npm/package.json DESCRIBES the package, registry.npmjs.org IS the package.

ops/npm/publish.mjs cannot run right now, and correctly so: it gates on the staged component matching the live origin byte for byte, and 4f2b21d grew the component to 17,991 bytes while the origin still serves 14,048. The site has to deploy first. The gate is doing its job.

--- prior note, 2026-08-12 ---
RESOLVED 2026-08-12. Published as @kynth/tearline@0.1.0. The bare name `tearline` is NOT taken (registry.npmjs.org/tearline was still a clean 404) but it is UNREGISTERABLE: `npm publish` returns HTTP 403 "Package name too similar to existing package readline". That is npm's similarity/typo-squat filter, not a collision, and no amount of waiting changes it. The @kynth org already existed on the registry (it carries @kynth/api, @kynth/api-mcp, @kynth/ai-tools), so the scope preserves the product name exactly rather than mangling it to tearline-element or tear-line.

The published manifest is ops/npm/package.json, NOT the repo root package.json. The root manifest is the SITE's — it stays "private": true and it depends on next, react, posthog-js, lenis and sonner. Publishing it would have handed `npm i` six runtime dependencies against a package whose first line promises zero. The published package has zero dependencies and four files (tearline.js, README.md, LICENSE, package.json), 21.3 kB unpacked.

A REAL BUG WAS CAUGHT ON THE WAY. src/tearline.js — the file the root manifest's `main` pointed at — was 340 lines / 12,756 bytes, while public/tearline.js and the live origin were 370 lines / 14,048 bytes. The 2026-08-06 commit b76c925 that added the `tearline:stage` export events edited public/ only, so `main` had been two weeks stale and a naive publish would have shipped a component OLDER than the playground serves, silently. src/ has been synced from public/ (both now sha256 96debf4e…). ops/npm/publish.mjs is the gate that makes it unrepeatable: it fetches the live /tearline.js and REFUSES to publish unless the staged file, src/tearline.js and the origin are all the same bytes.

SURFACES STILL CARRYING THE OLD CLAIM. README.md, public/llms.txt and src/app/share-image-custom-element/page.tsx were corrected on 2026-08-12. The npm CTA has NOT been restored to SiteHeader.tsx, HeroSection.tsx, InstallSection.tsx, SiteFooter.tsx, page.tsx or docs/page.tsx — those rows were deliberately REMOVED on 2026-07-29 rather than reworded, and putting an `npm i` row back into the header, hero and install section is a copy and layout decision for Isaiah, not a factual patch. claims.note: Fetched from the Spotify Web API reference on 2026-08-02. The time_range descriptions are quoted verbatim on the page. Load-bearing for the page's central observation — that the "last month / 6 months / all time" and "top 10 / top 50" controls shared by every receipt generator are the API's parameter list showing through the UI, not a design convention.
